sentences.text: Jangam Sivaiah, vs The State Of Telangana.

Rep. By Its ... on 7
August, 2024
 The Hon'Ble Sri Justice C. V. Bhaskar Reddy
 Writ Petition No.22792 of 2015
Order:

This Writ Petition, under Article 226 of the Constitution of India, is filed by the petitioners, seeking the following relief:
"...to Issue an appropriate writ, order or direction more particularly one in the nature of Mandamus declaring the action of the respondents in not paying the compensation for the lands of the petitioners viz 1st petitioner in Sy.No.307 to an extent of Ac.1.00 cents 2nd petitioner in Sy.No.442 to an extent of Ac.0.35 cents 3rd,4th, 5th, 6th, 7th petitioners in Sy.No.437 to an extent Ac.3.00 cents, Ac.2.00 cents and Ac.2.00 cents,
Ac.2.50 cents and Ac.2.50 cents respectively 8th, 9th, 10th, 11th, 12th, 19th petitioners in Sy.No.421 Ac.4.00 Cents, Ac.1.05 Cents and Ac.1.00 Cents, Ac.2.07 cents, Ac.450 cents, Ac.1.00 Cents and Ac.1.00 Cents, Ac.2.50 Cents respectively

13th petitioner in Sy.No.437/46 to an extent of Ac.3.50 Cents 14th petitioner in Sy.No.437/39 to an extent of Ac.4.00 cents 15th petitioner in Sy.No.437/30 to an extent of Ac.3.00 Cents 16th petitioner in Sy.No.437/29 and 236/E to an extent of Ac.2.00 Cents and Ac.2.00 cents 17th petitioner in Sy.No.410 to an extent of Ac.3.40 Cents 18th petitioner in Sy.No.437/38 to an extent of Ac.3.50 Cents in of Chagadona village, Ghattu Mandal, Mahabubnagar District, inundated in the Muchonipally Balancing Reservoir, on the ground that petitioners lands are assigned lands even though it is settled Law that petitioners are entitled for full compensation as per Mekala Pandu case reported in 2004 (2) ALT 546 (LB) as confirmed by the Supreme Court in Civil Appeal Nos.9317 - 9321 of 2012 as illegal, arbitrary, violative of Article 14, 21 & 300-A of the Constitution of India and consequently direct the respondents to pay full compensation by initiating proceedings under The Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 and pass..."
2.

entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Heard Sri B. Shiva Rama Sharma, learned counsel representing K. Ratanga Pani Reddy, learned counsel for the petitioners and learned Government Pleader for Land Acquisition and perused the record.
3. The case of the petitioners is that they are the landless poor persons belonging to weaker sections.

The State Government assigned lands viz 1st petitioner in Sy.No.307 to an extent of Ac.1.00 cents 2nd petitioner in Sy.No.442 to an extent of Ac.0.35 cents 3rd, 4th, 5th, 6th and 7th petitioners in Sy.No.437 to an extent Ac.3.00 cents, Ac.2.00 cents and Ac.2.00 cents, Ac.2.50 cents and Ac.2.50 cents respectively 8th, 9th, 10th, 11th, 12th and 19th petitioners in Sy.No.421 Ac.4.00 Cents, Ac.1.05 Jangam Sivaiah, vs The State Of Telangana.

13th petitioner in Sy.No.437/46 to an extent of Ac.3.50 Cents 14th petitioner in Sy.No.437/39 to an extent of Ac.4.00 cents 15th petitioner in Sy.No.437/30 to an extent of Ac.3.00 Cents 16th petitioner in Sy.No.437/29 and 236/E to an extent of Ac.2.00 Cents and Ac.2.00 cents 17th petitioner in Sy.No.410 to an extent of Ac.3.40 Cents 18th petitioner in Sy.No.437/38 to an extent of Ac.3.50 Cents.

The Government also issued Patta Certificates in terms of G.O.Ms.No.406,
dated 27.05.1958 and thereafter, their names were recorded in the Revenue records as the assignees/pattadars of the said lands.

It is the further case of the petitioners that their names were mutated as per the provisions of Record of Rights in Land and Pattadar Passbooks Act, 1971 and the entries made in 1b register depicts name of petitioners as pattadars.
4.

The grievance of the petitioners is that the respondents without initiating any proceedings under the provisions of Land Acquisition Act, 1894 or under the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement (RFCTLARR) Act, 2013 are making efforts to forcibly dispossess the petitioners, from the subject lands.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement (RFCTLARR) Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 5. Sri B. Shiva Rama Sharma, learned counsel representing K. Ratanga Pani Reddy, learned counsel for the petitioners has vehemently contended that since the petitioners are the assignees of the subject lands, they are entitled for compensation on par with the pattadars as held by the Larger Bench of this Court in Lao-Cum- Revenue Divisional Officer vs Mekala Pandu And Ors 1 (1 Supra).

entities.text: Lao-Cum- Revenue Divisional Officer vs Mekala Pandu And Ors 1 (1 Supra)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
6. Learned Government Pleader for Land Acquisition relying on the instructions furnished in File No.B/117/2005, dated 31.07.2015 has submitted that a complaint has been received from the villagers to the Office of the District Collector, dated 26.04.2008, stating that some of the mediators have created bogus certificates relating to title documents and trying to get ex-gratia as if they are the original 1 2004 (2) ALT 546 (LB) assignees of the lands under the provisions of G.O.Ms.No.1307,
Rev (Assignment-I) Department, dated 23.12.1993.
7.

In view of the submissions made by both the learned counsel, the writ petition is disposed of directing the respondents to conclude the enquiry in respect of the subject lands and pay compensation to the eligible pattadars/assignees as per the law laid down by the Larger Bench of this Court in the case of (1 Supra) within a period of six (06) months from the date of receipt of the copy of the order.
There shall be no order as to costs.

As a sequel thereto, miscellaneous petitions, if any, pending shall stand closed.
___________________________ C.V. BHASKAR REDDY, J Date: 07.08.2024 vsu Jangam Sivaiah, vs The State Of Telangana.
